AM8F-01.note: -9 is the (-2)^2 -> -4 sign slip, 11 is the -3x sign slip. Correct opener for a form that rises.

AM8F-02.note: 56 = g(5)-g(2) (index slip, fine). 46 maps to no wrong path I can construct - g(5)-g(3) is 48, g(4)-g(1) is 28. Weak option.

AM8F-05.note: 48 is the classic 8 + 10(5) - 10 off-by-one; 45 and 50 cover the other two index errors. Good set.

AM8F-06.note: 85 = C(150), 49 = 25 + 24 (the student who adds the fixed fee back). Both real.

AM8F-07.note: 13 = f(g(3)) is the order-reversal, the one distractor that matters here.

AM8F-08.solved: (x-3)^2 >= 0, so the minimum is 5 at x = 3.
AM8F-08.note: 3 (the x-coordinate offered as the value) is the live trap.

AM8F-09.solved: 2c - 7 = 15 -> c = 11; f(14) = 28 - 7 = 21. (Or: slope 2 over a run of 3 adds 6 to 15.)
AM8F-09.note: 18 = 15 + 3 (adds the run, not slope*run); 11 = c itself. Both real paths.

AM8F-10.note: 2.8 = f(4), the student who reads f^-1 as 'just evaluate'. 6.67 = 20/3 (drops the +2). Strong set.

AM8F-11.note: 28 = numerator only, 7 = denominator only. 6 I cannot source to a clean wrong path.

AM8F-12.note: 45 = the total bill, and the stem's final clause ('for the minutes used beyond 300') is what keeps it from being defensible. 32 = 800(0.04). Strong.

AM8F-13.solved: r^2 = 162/18 = 9; every term positive so r = 3; a5 = 162(3) = 486.
AM8F-13.note: The 'every term is positive' clause is load-bearing - without it r = -3 gives -486, not an option, so exclusivity holds either way. 180 = 162 + 18 (treats it as arithmetic).

AM8F-15.note: 97,200 = 3^5 (off-by-one triplings), 3,600 = 3^2, 4,800 = 400 x 3 x 4 (multiplies instead of exponentiates). All three are real student paths.

AM8F-16.note: 3 = h/6 left unmultiplied, 48 = 6 x 8. 24 is the fourth halving. Reasonable.

AM8F-17.solved: x - 3 inside shifts right 3; +4 outside shifts up 4. (2,-5) -> (5,-1).
AM8F-17.note: The options are the full 2x2 sign grid, which is exactly right for this item type.

AM8F-18.solved: x^2 - 9 = 0 at x = 3 and x = -3; only 3 is offered.
AM8F-18.note: -5 (numerator zero, confuses undefined with zero) is the good one; -9 and 9 are filler.

AM8F-19.solved: sin x has minimum -1, so f min = 4(-1) + 3 = -1.
AM8F-19.note: -7 = -4 - 3 (sign slip on the +3), -4 = amplitude alone, 7 = the maximum. Solid.

AM8F-20.note: Stem says 'The functions f and h are defined by' and then introduces g mid-sentence without declaring it - sloppy but not ambiguous. 23 = h(4), 13 = f(4).

AM8F-21.solved: g(x) = 0 means f(x) = 10, true at x = -3 and x = 2; greatest is 2.
AM8F-21.note: 'every value of the function f' is doing necessary work - it closes the domain so 2 is provably the greatest. -3 (the other preimage) is the intended trap; 10 and 19 are outputs offered as inputs, weak.

AM8F-22.note: 25 = 50/2 (treats the two terms as equal), 17 = a3, 5 = an off-by-one on the index offsets. Good.

AM8F-23.note: Ordering oddity: AM8F-23 sits between -19 and -20 in the render. On a form that rises, the id order and the position order should agree. 5 = the axis itself, the best distractor here.

AM8F-24.note: 25,000 is the arithmetic midpoint and is the whole point of the item; 22,500 = half of 45,000. Strong set - this is the best-distractored item in the batch.

AM8F-25.note: 27 = 3(9), 1 = (9-6)/3 with the sign flipped, 15 = 9 + 6. All three are the standard direction errors.

AM8F-26.solved: Need x - 4 to divide 12. Over integer x in [0,10] with x != 4, x-4 runs -4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4,5,6; of these all but 5 divide 12. That is 9 values (x = 0,1,2,3,5,6,7,8,10).
AM8F-26.note: Genuinely hard by the stated rule: nothing in the stem says the divisors may be negative, and a student who lists only the positive divisors of 12 lands exactly on option B (5). 10 is 'all of them but x=4'. This is the strongest item in the batch.

AM8F-27.note: Hard, but the weakest of the three I grade hard: the unstated noticing is only that a negative argument wraps FORWARD by a period, and a student who reduces mod 6 mechanically gets there without noticing anything. 15 = 9 + 6 (sign lost on g(4)); 9 = g(50) with g(-2) read as 0.

AM8F-28.solved: 19.25 - 8.00 = 11.25 charged in additional-pound units; 11.25/1.25 = 9 units. Because a part of a pound is billed as a whole one, 9 units cover any weight above 3+8 = 11 up to and including 3+9 = 12. Greatest possible weight = 12.
AM8F-28.note: Hard and correctly so: the stem never says the charge is a step function, so 'greatest possible' has to be recognised as inverting a ceiling. Option D (9) is where a student who does the arithmetic and stops lands; 11.25 is the remainder; 15.4 = 19.25/1.25. Note this shares its whole shell with -06 and -12 (fixed fee plus per-unit rate) and is the only one of the three with an idea in it.
